summary: When the CI gate would judge the merge tree (the branch is more than HEAD_TREE_MAX_BEHIND commits behind main, or protected files moved on main since the branch point), st-test now merges the base into the branch after its wait for a pool tree and signs the merged head's own tree, which stays valid for 24 more main commits, instead of a merge tree that main's next commit voids; with --push it pushes the branch at that merge

replay.detail: No record, signature or storage format changes.

rules.detail: The gate's rule is unchanged: st-test asks the base's branch_point_verdict as before and only changes which commit it signs.

compatibility.detail: A signing run that hears fallback now adds a merge commit to the caller's branch (with the caller's git identity) and, with --push and exit 0, pushes that branch to the same-named branch on the remote; it stops on a conflict, on uncommitted tracked changes, and when the remote branch has commits the local one lacks. A detached HEAD or a branch named as the base's is not pushed. --status and --seed change nothing. st-test re-executes the base's copy, so this applies to every branch once it merges.

recovery.detail: Revert the change; a merge commit st-test made is an ordinary merge of main and needs no cleanup.
